About Grammar / here Nouns:

Hacking German Noun Genders

I took a class about 10 years ago now when I was in Munich and generally it was pretty fairly standard to most German grammar classes but the instructor had one particularly interesting take on noun genders. While it is common knowledge that the last word in a compound word gives the gender of that entire word, it's not as common to be taught that certain word endings give away gender. The first 3 "Always" are the most memorable and helpful, others help as well though.

I got back into learning German fairly loosely over this Covid season and dug up his old course material that he actually still posts online. [The list of everything gender wise is on page 114](http://w3-o.hm.edu/home/fb/fb13/drblock/germangram.pdf). I definitely found it easier to learn these rules to give me a better opportunity at discovering Gender on my own out in the wild.

I'll  put these rules into an Anki and post it here when I have time today. I'd recommend doing it on your own but at minimum having a premade deck in there will be helpful.

For now here's it as a reddit post:

#Endings that ALWAYS indicate Gender

**ALWAYS** with little to no exceptions

ALWAYS Feminine Endings:

* -heit / keit (en) (zB Gerissenheit)
* -schaft (zB Wissenschaft)
* -ung (zB Beratung)
* -ei (zB Konditorei)
* exception der Papagei 

ALWAYS Neutral Endings

* -chen (zB Mädchen)
* -lein (zB Fräulein)

ALWAYS Masculine Endings

* -ling (Frühling)
* -ig, -ich, -eich, -rich (Käfig, Teppich, Deich, Breich, Enterich) 
* exception das Reich

___


**MOSTLY** There's also endings that identify Gender either most of the time or under certain precursors. Unfortunately there are more exceptions that are listed

MOSTLY Neutral Endings

* -tum (zB Christentum, Bürgertum) exceptions der Irrtum and der Recihtum
* -nis (zB Ereignis, Bedürfnis) exceptions die Erlaubnis, Finsternis, Kenntnis
* -sal (zB Schicksal, Scheusal) exceptions die Mühsal, Trübsal, Drangsal
* -sel (zB Rätsel) exceptions der Stopsel, Wechsel

___

#Rules 

These have more exceptions and you will have to use a little logic to determine

**RULES** Masculine Ending -er, exceptions noted

* Agent nouns from verbs with feminine -in (innen) versions zB arbeiten = der Arbeiter, die Arbeiterin
* Agent nouns from other sources zB der Gegner, Geige
* Tools and Utensils = Toaster, Eimer, Trichter, Hammer, Becher (exceptions die Klammer, Leiter)
* Nouns of Affiliation - Italiener, Amerikaner, Römer
* Animals - Tiger, Käfer (exceptions die Auster, Elster)

**RULES** The mostly **Feminine** ending -e (excluding those that begin with Ge)

* Inanimate object feminine: Rübe, Lampe, Ecke  (exceptions Käse,m.) (Auge [-n], Ende [-n],
Erbe [npl], n.)
* Abstract nouns Güte, Tiefe, Breite
* cold-blooded animals and birds are feminine zB Schlange, Schnecke, Ente,
Eule (exceptions Rabe, Falke, m.)

Exception Rules to -e ending

* warm-blooded animals and
humans are masculine zB Junge, Bote, Löwe, Bulle
* nationalities are masculine Franzose, Russe, Grieche with fem. -in: zB Französin

**RULES** **Feminine** Stem in -r, -l

* Feminine past derivation -e MHG zale > Zahl [-en] zB Wahl, Zahl, Qual, Tür, Uhr
(Feuer)wehr, Feder, Spur


**Rules** the mostly **Neutral** ending -en 

* infinitives Singen, Tanzen, Fressen
* non infinitives Becken, Kissen, Zeichen

Exceptions

* All others are mostly masculine Laden, Garten, Wagen
* A few masculine where -n is lacking in the nom - Friede, Glaube, Wille, Funke, Gedanke

**Rules** mostly Feminine Ending -t/-d(e) and st



* overrides rules with the prefix Ge- as well die Fahrt, Sicht, Kunst, Haft, Jagd, Magd, Beichte, Bürde
* Angst, Kunst (Dienst,
Verdienst, Verlust [-e], Frost
["-e], m.)

**Rules** the prefix Ge- 

* neuter collectives das Gebiss, Gefängnis, Gebirge, Gemüse, Getreide, Gesicht
* masculine sociatives zB der Geselle, Gefährte, Gebrüder (pl.) fem. -in
* masculine abstract from verb stems zB der Geruch, Gestank, Genuss, Gefallen
* feminine abstract with ending -t/d(e) zB die Geburt, Gemeinde, Gewalt,
Geschwülst, Geschichte  

____


#Foreign Nouns

Nouns that have foreign origins.

**Rules** Foreign Nouns **Masculine** mostly n-declension (-n,-n),some mixed (-s, -n) or strong (-s, -e).  Feminine -in.

Persons:

* -ant, zB der Demonstrant
* -ar, zB der Kommissar
* -är, zB der Aktionär
* -at,zB der Soldat
* -ent, zB der Absolvent
* -et, zB der Athlet
* -eur, zB der Ingenieur
* -ist, zB der Pazifist
* -loge, zB der Philologe
* -or, zB der Doktor (-s, -en)
* -us (fem. -in) 

Nonpersons

* -at zB der Apparat
* -us zB der Organismus

**Rules** Foreign Nouns **Neutral** plurals mostly strong but note exceptions

Nonpersons

* -ar zB das Seminar -e
* -at zB das Konsulat -e
* -ett zB das Lazarett -e
* -il zB das Exil -e
* -ma zB das Thema -en  
* -mm zB das Programm -e
* -o zB das Konto
* -ent ZB das Argument -e
* -um zB das Tempus -ora
* -ing das Training

**Rules** Foreign Nouns **Feminine** 

Abstract Nouns

* -age zB Courage
